name: malicious-cocoa-daemon
description: Practice-box persistence finding: installs and enables a long-running background 'sync daemon' whose live process must actually be found and stopped -- unlike cocoa-update.service (Type=oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes), this unit is Type=simple with Restart=on-failure, so a real PID persists and respawns unless the service itself is stopped/disabled, not just its unit file deleted.
script:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

mkdir -p /opt/.cocoa-daemon
cat > /opt/.cocoa-daemon/cocoa-daemon <<'PAYLOAD'
#!/bin/sh
# Harmless training payload: a real, continuously-running process (not
# oneshot) -- the finding is that it must be killed/stopped, not just its
# unit file deleted. Heartbeats to a log so its activity is forensically visible.
while true; do
    printf '%s\n' "cocoa-daemon heartbeat" >> /var/log/cocoa-sync.log
    sleep 30
done
PAYLOAD
chmod 0700 /opt/.cocoa-daemon/cocoa-daemon
chmod 0700 /opt/.cocoa-daemon

cat > /etc/systemd/system/cocoa-sync.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Cocoa sync daemon (training finding)
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/opt/.cocoa-daemon/cocoa-daemon
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
chmod 0644 /etc/systemd/system/cocoa-sync.service
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable --now cocoa-sync.service
fi
